subject: Sales discovery: model fit & eval \u0014 next steps / regression concern
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@retailco.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-22T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sales discovery: model fit & eval  next steps

Thanks for the call today, Alex  glad we had a chance to walk through the RetailCo objectives. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

Summary from today
- Goal: deploy assistant for category-level product recommendations and customer support triage.
- Primary metrics: top-1 recommendation accuracy, deflection rate, and CSAT for templated responses.
- Constraints: sub-second latency for chat flows; data residency in us-east-1.

Recommended follow-ups (next 4872h)
1) You send sample prompt set + 200 representative examples (happy you can share a redacted subset).
2) We run a short eval suite (model fit + prompt sensitivity) and share a results summary and recommended model variants.
3) If model/results look reasonable, we propose a canary pin/AB test before a full rollout.

Attachments: please send the prompt set (CSV) and a few edge-case examples. I attached a one-pager on our evaluation framework for context.

Next steps from me: Vivek will scope the evaluation and recommend model variants; Lauren will follow up on pricing + Dedicated capacity options.

Thanks  talk soon.


Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_evals_overview.pdf (PDF, 48KB)]

From: Alex Johnson <alex@retailco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@retailco.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sales discovery: model fit & eval  next steps

Thanks Marissa  great call. Attached is a redacted CSV of the prompt set (samples across categories + support transcripts). We also included a short file with a few failing examples we've seen in prod.

Files attached:
- RetailCo_prompt_set_v1.csv
- regression_examples.txt

Two quick notes:
- We prioritize retail product taxonomy correctness  false positives on category mapping are the biggest issue.
- We currently use a hosted model from another provider but are evaluating cost/latency tradeoffs.

Can you run your evals against the prompt set and share the result by EOD tomorrow? Happy to hop on another call if useful.


Alex Johnson
Head of ML Eng, RetailCo
alex@retailco.com
[Attachment: RetailCo_prompt_set_v1.csv (CSV, 120KB)]
[Attachment: regression_examples.txt (TXT, 4KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@retailco.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-23T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sales discovery: model fit & eval  next steps

Appreciate the prompt set, Alex  we ran the initial eval pass this morning. High level findings attached (model_evals_summary.pdf) and a short note below.

Summary of results (initial)
- Top candidates: redwood/opt-7b-v1 (balanced accuracy / cost), redwood/opt-13b-q8 (higher-quality for taxonomy mapping), redwood/llama-2-7b-pt (fastest, lower cost but weaker on edge cases).
- Recommendation: start with opt-7b-v1 for a canary (good latency / token cost balance), run a targeted subset of taxonomy edge cases on opt-13b-q8.
- Observed failure modes: long product lists cause hallucinated categories; short descriptions sometimes default to generic categories.

Links and artifacts
- Full eval report: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-model-evals
- Prompt set we used: RetailCo_prompt_set_v1.csv (attached)

Proposed next steps
1) Approve a 48-hour canary on opt-7b-v1 pinned for RetailCo with AB-test against your current model.
2) If opt-7b-v1 passes taxonomy thresholds, schedule a rollout plan + cost estimate (Lauren).

I've attached the summary PDF and included a small set of examples we think are good canary tests. Let us know if you'd like to expand the test set.


Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: model_evals_summary.pdf (PDF, 92KB)]

From: Alex Johnson <alex@retailco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@retailco.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-24T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sales discovery: model fit & eval  regression concern

Quick update: we started the canary test this morning but noticed an unexpected regression on our taxonomy mapping when comparing the new variant to our baseline. Examples below (baseline -> new):

- "women's running shoes > sneakers" -> baseline: "Running Shoes" | opt-7b-v1: "Shoes" (loss of specificity)
- "eco-friendly bamboo toothbrush" -> baseline: "Oral Care" | opt-7b-v1: "Bathroom"

These are causing degraded downstream metrics (lower top-1 accuracy on our evaluation harness). We're capturing logs and adding them to regression_examples.txt. Can you check if this is expected given the model variant, or if there's a prompt set / temperature tweak we should try?

Time sensitivity: we have a limited promotion window next week, so we need to decide whether to proceed with the canary or roll back to the baseline model.


Alex Johnson
Head of ML Eng, RetailCo
[Attachment: regression_examples.txt (TXT, 6KB)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@retailco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-24T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Sales discovery: model fit & eval  regression concern

Thanks Alex  appreciate the quick signal and the examples. Short answers up front:
1) This looks like a prompt-sensitivity / calibration issue rather than a catastrophic model bug.
2) We can pin RetailCo to opt-7b-v1 but also run an immediate AB where 80% traffic goes to your baseline and 20% to opt-7b-v1 with more targeted temperature/prompt templates.
3) If you want a quick rollback to baseline, we can pin to your previous model (v2.3) within ~30 minutes  we'll preserve logs and run a diff after the rollback.

Proposed plan (recommended)
- Short-term (next 24h): Pin traffic back to baseline (v2.3) to stabilize the promotion window.
- Parallel work: we will run a focused sensitivity sweep on the failing examples (temp, prompt prefixes, instruction tuning) and test opt-13b-q8 on the taxonomy subset.
- Deliverables: regression diff (examples + token-level traces), a small prompt-set patch, and a suggested pin policy (pin to v2.3 or pin opt-7b-v1 with prompt patches).

Marissa / Lauren  if RetailCo approves, we'll execute the rollback/pin today. Alex  can you confirm you'd prefer rollback now or continue the controlled AB?


Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineering (Inference)
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: rollback_playbook.md (MD, 8KB)]
